references.text: God promises Moses that He will be with him, the same promise of divine presence given here regarding his mouth.
God promises to raise up a prophet and put His words in his mouth, the same motif of God giving words to the one who speaks.
The Lord puts His words in the prophet's mouth, parallel to the promise to be with Moses' mouth and teach him what he should say.
The Lord touches Jeremiah's mouth and puts His words there, the same concept of divine guidance in speech.
God opens Ezekiel's mouth to speak, a similar theme of God controlling and guiding the prophet's speech.
Jesus promises the disciples that they should not worry about what to say, for the Spirit will give them the words, the same promise of divine guidance in speech.
The Holy Spirit will teach the disciples what they should say, parallel to God's promise to teach Moses what he should speak.
Jesus promises to give the disciples words and wisdom when they must defend themselves, the same motif of divine assistance in speech.
A direct theological parallel regarding God's promise to give words at the moment of speaking, where the New Testament fulfills the Old Testament promise with the role of the Holy Spirit.
